tools.name: get_user_info
tools.description: Get the TikTok Business account the stored access token belongs to. Check the returned code: 0 means success, any other value is an API error carried in an HTTP 200 body

tools.name: get_advertiser_info
tools.description: Get the advertiser account held in the stored credential (name, status, currency, timezone). Check the returned code: 0 means success

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: List campaigns in the advertiser account held in the stored credential, with objective, budget and delivery status. Check the returned code: 0 means success

page_size.description: Max campaigns to return per page (default 20, max 100)

tools.name: list_adgroups
tools.description: List ad groups in the advertiser account held in the stored credential, with campaign, budget, bidding and delivery status. Check the returned code: 0 means success

page_size.description: Max ad groups to return per page (default 20, max 100)

tools.name: list_ads
tools.description: List ads in the advertiser account held in the stored credential, with their ad group, campaign and delivery status. Check the returned code: 0 means success

page_size.description: Max ads to return per page (default 20, max 100)

tools.name: get_campaign_report
tools.description: Get a basic per-campaign performance report (spend, impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC) for a date range in the advertiser account held in the stored credential. Check the returned code: 0 means success

start_date.description: First day of the report window, YYYY-MM-DD, in the advertiser's timezone

end_date.description: Last day of the report window, YYYY-MM-DD, in the advertiser's timezone

page_size.description: Max rows to return per page (default 20, max 100)

needs_review: READ THIS BEFORE READING THE PROOF FILE. TikTok Business answers EVERY call with HTTP 200 and carries the real outcome in the body's code field, so the shape-proof harness (which classifies on status first, by design) flags each probe no_auth_required + public_endpoint and classes the spec SHAPE_PROVEN. THOSE TWO FLAGS ARE WRONG: these endpoints are not public and auth IS enforced. The verbatim bodies from the 2026-09-12 authoring probes, each returned with HTTP 200: GET /open_api/v1.3/user/info/ -> {"code":40105,"message":"Access token is incorrect or has been revoked.","request_id":"2026091211303580A49213BFDAAE5DD752"} · GET /open_api/v1.3/adgroup/get/?advertiser_id=123 -> {"code": 40105, "message": "Access token is incorrect or has been revoked.", "request_id": "2026091211323223B2360CD3C841D7A31D", "data": {}} · GET /open_api/v1.3/ad/get/?advertiser_id=123 -> {"code": 40105, "message": "Access token is incorrect or has been revoked.", "request_id": "20260912113233DC91E785230CE268F1FF", "data": {}}. Read the overall class as AMBIGUOUS: host, TLS, base_url, the Access-Token header name and the paths are evidenced, and auth rejection is evidenced IN THE BODY, but the harness's status-based matrix cannot express that and no classification here was hand-edited.

Where the dummy credential is not a valid integer, TikTok's own parameter validation answers first, still with HTTP 200: GET /open_api/v1.3/campaign/get/?advertiser_id=QUOXSHAPEPROOFDUMMYADVERTISERID -> {"code": 40002, "message": "advertiser_id: Not a valid integer or integer-string.", "request_id": "2026091211323155EC9DDBBA68A43682F7", "data": {}} and GET /open_api/v1.3/advertiser/info/?advertiser_ids=["QUOXSHAPEPROOFDUMMYADVERTISERID"] -> {"code": 40002, "message": "advertiser_ids.0: Not a valid integer or integer-string.", "request_id": "20260912113230C6D033D7618573218330", "data": {}}. A per-endpoint parameter error proves the request reached that endpoint's own handler. The control path answers HTTP 404 with an nginx-style HTML page (

404 Not Found

...
TLB
), so routed API paths ARE distinguishable from unrouted ones here; that distinction is documented rather than claimed as a class. No advertiser_id _probe hint can help, because _probe may only substitute tool inputs, never a credential field, and inventing a stranger's real advertiser ID would be worse.

Because the transport status is always 200, every tool picks code and message into its output and every description tells the caller to check code: 0. Without that an API-level failure would reach an agent as an empty-looking success, which is the same defect class as an error body read as data.

Scaffolded auth (header Access-Token, no Bearer prefix) and the scaffolded test block both stand unchanged, and the header name is PROVEN to be the one TikTok reads: the same call with the token under a different header name, and with no token header at all, both answer {"code":40104,"message":"The access_token is empty."} (HTTP 200), while the token under Access-Token reaches the token check itself and answers code 40105 'Access token is incorrect or has been revoked.' The 40104 / 40105 split is what distinguishes a header TikTok read from one it never saw. static_headers carries only Accept: application/json (GET reads send no body).

READ-ONLY by design: no tool is marked write:true. /campaign/create/, /campaign/update/, /adgroup/create/ and /ad/status/update/ are all POST endpoints on the same host and are deliberately not modelled.

No response body was ever data: the proof stops at TikTok's auth and parameter errors, so every path, query parameter and picked field name comes from the Marketing API v1.3 reference, not from a live 2xx. Field naming is the softest part: advertiser/info/ returns the account name as name in v1.3 (it was advertiser_name in v1.2), and report rows nest their values under dimensions.* and metrics.*. A wrong pick source yields an empty value silently, so the first run with a real token must confirm them.

get_campaign_report carries a _probe hint (start_date 2026-09-01, end_date 2026-09-02) so the blind probe sends real-shaped dates and reaches the auth check instead of stopping at a date-format error. Report windows, dimensions and metrics are fixed to a basic per-campaign set: report_type BASIC, data_level AUCTION_CAMPAIGN, dimensions [campaign_id], metrics spend/impressions/clicks/ctr/cpc. Lifetime queries, hourly granularity and audience dimensions are not exposed.

page is clamped 1 to 100 and page_size 20 to 100 (TikTok documents a page_size ceiling of 1000; the lower cap is a deliberate response-size guard, paired with truncate 2000). rateLimit 30/min is a local courtesy and spend guard chosen here, not a documented TikTok ceiling: TikTok rate limits per app and per endpoint rather than publishing one per-minute number.
